definitions.meaning: to fail to hit or to skip something, as in skipping a meeting
a young unmarried woman, the title used before her name

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: the verb for failing to catch or dodging, and the old title for a young unmarried woman.

parts.note: a handful sounds like a troublesome guest, but it is literally a fistful of paper scraps thrown over the newlyweds

explanation.surface: Someone difficult at a wedding, a guest who is a real handful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A handful' idiomatically means a troublesome person; here it means what fits in a hand, the paper pieces tossed at the bride and groom.
explanation.definitionFit: Guests throw fistfuls of small coloured paper pieces over a couple after the ceremony.

definitions.meaning: a knitted pullover worn on the upper body
the largest of the Channel Islands, between England and France

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a knitted pullover garment, and the Channel Island that gave the garment its name.

indicators.note: laying waste to the letters wrecks their order so they are rebuilt as something new

explanation.surface: Paying ten pounds for a bowl of miso soup is money thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste of' looks like a complaint about the price; it signals rearranging TENNER and MISO. A tenner is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian thick vegetable broth with pasta or rice, a classic example of a soup.

clue.text: State north Australia backs in song

indicators.note: the reversed pair sits inside the word for a song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: backs means goes backwards, so the letters for north and Australia are read right to left

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A song in which an American state is sung about by northern Australians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns NOZ into ZON, which goes inside ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A south-western US state of the union, home of the Grand Canyon.

clue.text: In general, a mournful site of battle

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words general, a mournful

explanation.surface: A general describing a sad battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texas mission where a famous 1836 siege and battle took place.

clue.text: Commercial break aired, TV set getting people hooked

indicators.note: people hooked are caught and held inside the shuffled letters
breaking the words aired and TV set scatters their letters for reassembly

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for people

explanation.surface: A TV commercial break comes on and viewers are glued to the set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial break' reads as one phrase, but 'Commercial' is the definition and 'break' rearranges AIRED TV SET into ADVERTISET; MEN goes inside it near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial is a noun for a paid promotional broadcast, a television promotion.

clue.text: Old Testament priest, by Old Testament author

parts.note: Eli was the priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A biblical priest standing next to a scripture writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'author' seems to belong to Old Testament, but it is the definition: George Eliot or T S Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot the novelist and T S Eliot the poet both bear this surname of writers.

clue.text: Terrible fate drinking beer — bit gone to pot?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take the beer in, holding it inside
something terrible is in a bad way, so the letters of fate are scrambled

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A grim fate befalls a drinker, a person who has gone to pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone to pot' means ruined, but literally a scrap of tea goes into the teapot. 'Terrible' rearranges the letters of 'fate' to TEAF, and 'drinking' puts the beer inside them. In Cockney rhyming slang, a tea leaf is also a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A single leaf of tea is a small bit that is put into the teapot for brewing.

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic eucharistic service
if means on condition that

explanation.surface: A church service held on condition that the mountains allow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A geological term for a compact group of mountains, a mountain range or block.

indicators.note: improvising on the keyboards means playing freely with the letters of claviers

explanation.surface: Improvising on keyboard instruments is a gut-level art.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling from the gut rather than reason, an intuitive deep-seated response.

clue.text: Confused story put out, vexing you initially

indicators.note: put out of order, the letters of story put are rearranged
the opening letters of vexing and you are taken

explanation.surface: A muddled tale gets told and annoys you from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like a phrase meaning upset. Only 'out' signals the anagram, and 'put' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Upside down and in total disorder, so jumbled or muddled up.

indicators.note: used as a verb, fragments means breaks into pieces, so the letters of shattering are broken up

explanation.surface: Tidying up the broken bits after something smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattering' looks like the anagram signal and 'fragments' the fodder; it is the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To put in order or tidy, making something orderly and level.

indicators.note: inspiring literally breathes in, so the number takes the letter inside

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure

indicators.note: primarily means first, picking the opening letter of exasperation

explanation.surface: A teenager is a figure who causes exasperation.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent aged thirteen to nineteen is a young person.

indicators.note: discussed means spoken of, so the words are taken as they sound

parts.note: Richmond is the capital of Virginia, so a wolf from there is a Virginian wolf

explanation.surface: A writer talks about a predator from Richmond.
explanation.walkthrough: Richmond is also a London suburb, near where she lived and founded the Hogarth Press; here it is the capital of the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The modernist English novelist who wrote Mrs Dalloway and To the Lighthouse.

clue.text: Very popular children's game, English classic

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
tag is the chasing game also called tig or it

explanation.surface: A much-loved playground game from England is a classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Of lasting high quality and from a notable past period, so of classic quality.

definitions.meaning: the 1815 defeat of Napoleon in Belgium
a major London railway terminus named after that battle

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: Napoleon's final battle and the big London rail terminus named after it.

indicators.note: the letters are contained in the words giant, indomitable

explanation.surface: A huge, unbeatable opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: One who is against something, an opposer or objector.

clue.text: Talk — as might Jack Sprat's wife?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for chatting idly at length
in the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat while his wife could eat no lean, so she would munch the fatty parts

explanation.surface: A conversational aside about the nursery-rhyme couple's eating habits.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat is from the English nursery rhyme: 'Jack Sprat could eat no fat, his wife could eat no lean'.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom meaning to chat or gossip at leisure, also literally to chomp on fatty meat.

definitions.meaning: fondue is melted cheese, so it is full of cheese

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: tacky and cheap-looking, and literally tasting of cheese.

clue.text: Suffering in the past ends in plain misery

parts.note: ago means in the past, as in years ago

indicators.note: the closing letters of plain and misery are taken

explanation.surface: Remembering past hardships, which ended in simple misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misery' tempts as the definition; it is fodder, and 'Suffering' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense pain or distress, the same as severe suffering.

parts.note: cash is money in coins and notes
mere means nothing more than, only

explanation.surface: Money is the only consideration in buying wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine soft goat's wool from Kashmir, used for luxury knitwear.

parts.note: ruby is a deep red colour
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: An alluring stolen ruby, hot property.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for extremely attractive or passionate, a fiery, alluring quality.

definitions.meaning: a serving of food on a plate

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: slang for an attractive person, and a prepared course served on a plate.

clue.text: Chance to delete first of numbers

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for those numbers is removed

parts.note: sevens are numbers

explanation.surface: A probability exercise in erasing the first of a set of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, even odds give a fifty-fifty chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting term for a one-to-one price, a fifty-fifty likelihood.

parts.note: trots means runs at a jog
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A communist goes jogging in Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was the Russian revolutionary and Marxist leader, an exemplary communist.
